build: PAL original, two-sided G64; level 1 load in play

comments.text: Entry of the level 1 file, jumped to by the resident loader at $0424. Sets up the title screen ($0A60), then loops between the credits page ($11BC) and the high-score page ($13C9), with pauses through $2027, until $0EEC sees fire and starts play.
A lone RTS, called first by the entry at $0A20.

Blanks the screen and switches the video chip to bank 3 ($DD00 bits 0-1 cleared), screen at $CC00 and characters at $E000 ($D018=$38), with extended colour mode on ($D011 bit 6), and banks out the ROMs ($01=$35).
The key code read every frame by $0E30.
Reads the keyboard with CIA 1 into A; returns at once when no line of the port reads low (the test at $0E3F), otherwise scans the rows from $0EA7. $1EF4 keeps the result in $0E2F.
Which attract page is up: 0 for the credits page, 1 for the high-score table.
Title loop step: polls the joystick byte $203B for fire (bit 4) and, every time the countdown in $203A and $2039 runs out, flips $0EEA to swap between the credits and score pages.

Screen-code text of the level 1 briefing: "LEVEL ONE", "DARKMAN SEEKING REVENGE ON THOSE WHO DISFIGURED HIM SETS OUT TO ACQUIRE THE ILL GOTTEN GAINS OF ROBERT G DURANT TO FURTHER HIS PLANS", ended by "END OF LINE".
Draws the credits page: the licence lines, the credits and "PRESS FIRE TO START" from the text at $1675.
"YOU HAVE ACHIEVED A HIGH SCORE" and, at $1357, "PLEASE ENTER YOUR NAME".
Title-screen step: while the NMI flag is clear and $0A13 holds $58, calls $1110.
Draws the "TODAYS TOP DARKMEN" high-score table.
Turns extended colour mode on (and multicolour in $D016) when $0A5F is set, off when it is clear.

Credits page text in screen codes: "TM AND COPYRIGHT 1990 UNIVERSAL CITY STUDIOS INC", the licence lines, "CODED BY FINLAY MUNRO", "GRAPHICS BY NOEL HINES", "SONICS BY JONATHAN DUNN", "PRODUCED BY TWILIGHT" and "PRESS FIRE TO START".
Pause: when the key code in $0E2F is $50, sets $1EF2, waits for the key to be released, pressed again and released, then clears $1EF2.

Main loop of play. Each pass runs $1FD5 (a bare RTS), redraws the panel's bar ($4449) and figures ($44FD), runs $1A0C and the pause check. Leaves for $4A8F when $1A1E is set, and for the end of the game ($195C, then $0F38) when $0A11 and $43E3 are both zero; otherwise waits for the NMI flag $2038.
End of play: tidies up ($18C5), blanks the screen, silences the sound ($B828), turns the sprites off, switches to a text screen at $CC00 and clears the key code.
"GAME OVER" in screen codes.

Start of play, from $0F35: blanks the screen, turns sprites off, clears the end-of-play flag $1A1E, pauses through $2027, banks the ROMs out and selects video bank 3 with $D018=$34, then sets up the play screen and interrupts.

Raster interrupt 3 of 4 in play. Sets the screen-matrix bits of $D018 to 3 (screen at $CC00) and ORs $D011 with $4F, which turns on extended colour mode; blacks the border and the sprite multicolours, counts down $29F4 and $29F3, and reads joystick port 2 ($DC00) into $203B whenever $29F3 is zero. Then selects the character set at $E000 ($D018 low bits $08), sets the next raster line to 205 and chains to $1DBF. The final LDA, LDX and LDY get their operands from the stores at the top: the saved registers are restored by self-modified code.

Raster interrupt 4 of 4 in play. After a run of NOPs that times the write to the raster line, sets bit 5 (bitmap) of $D011 and multicolour in $D016, blacks the border, sets the next interrupt for line 10 at $1E21, clears extended colour mode again, and unless the game is paused ($1EF2) calls $41EF, $4636 and $2066.

Raster interrupt 1 of 4 in play, on line 10. Acknowledges the video chip, sets the fine horizontal scroll from $1EF3, sets the colour mode ($1656) and the screen matrix ($1FA4), and turns sprites on unless $18C3 hides them. Then runs the play subsystems ($265E, $354A, $3725, and while not paused $4140 and $3190, then $3297), places Darkman's three sprites (0, 1 and 2) at the position held in $2657, $2659 and $2658, the second 21 lines lower, and colours them. Calls $4586 and $45C9 when not paused, and chains to $1EF4 on line 80.
1 while the game is paused ($1777); the interrupts skip the moving parts of the game while it is set.

Raster interrupt 2 of 4 in play, on line 80. Sets the scroll again and the background multicolours $0B and $0F, calls $1F40, plays the music and effects ($B176), reads the keyboard ($0E30) into $0E2F, and chains to $1D43 on line 198.
Selects the screen matrix through $D018: $30 (screen at $CC00) when $1D42 is set, $20 (screen at $C800) when it is clear, with the character set at $C000 either way. Two screens to flip between.
Mixes CIA 1's timer A, both bytes, with the previous result in $1FD4 and rotates it: a random number in $1FD4.
Starts with RTS, so it returns at once. The bytes after it would read CIA 2 port A bit 2 and drop the return address (PLA, PLA) when it is set; nothing reaches them while the RTS is there.
Pause used between the attract pages; called with A=$FF six times in a row from $0A3A.
Non-maskable interrupt: sets the flag $2038 to 1 and returns.
Set to 1 by every NMI ($2030); cleared and polled by the code that waits on it.
Joystick port 2 as last read by $1D43; bit 4 clear is fire.
Sets $2062 and, when $1D42 is set, copies rows of the screen at $CC00 to the one at $C800, one row of 40 bytes at a time; the copy behind the screen flip in $1FA4.
Darkman's horizontal position, low byte (with $2659 the ninth bit), written to sprites 0-2 by $1E21.
Darkman's vertical position, written to sprites 0 and 2 by $1E21; sprite 1 sits 21 lines below.
Ninth bit of Darkman's horizontal position.
Moves Darkman; skipped while paused. Begins by testing his position against the right edge ($D5 with the ninth bit) when $3638 is set.

Reads the stick for Darkman: clears his attack state ($2769, $276A, $312D), rounds his height in $2658 to the bottom of a character row (ORA #$07), counts down $2742, then tests left ($203B and $DC00 bit 2) and the other directions to choose a move.
Compares a record through the pointer $87/$88 with the values in $1A1F and $1A20, and when they match clears sprites 3 and 4's vertical positions and $33EA-$33EB.
Places the two enemies' sprites: sprites 3 and 4 for the first (from $3744, $3746 and $3748) and 5 and 6 for the second, each pair stacked 21 lines apart, and sets their colours.
Calls $384E and $421F for each of two slots (X=0, 1), unless paused, then $3639.
Per-enemy state, two slots; 0 and 5 mean the slot is not checked by $17CD.
Per-enemy horizontal position, two slots, with the ninth bit at $3746.
Per-enemy vertical position, two slots.
For enemy slot X: looks up the frame pointer for the state in $3742,X in the table at $38D9 and draws it through $3BEC.

For enemy slot X, when $2768 is 9 or $2F67 is 13 (values of Darkman's move state not yet named): compares the enemy's height in $3748,X with Darkman's in $2658 and, within 10 lines above or 24 below, goes on to the test at $4252.

Builds the panel's bar: fills a column of characters at $CF59 and their colour, writes a striped pattern into the eight character shapes at $4409, masks off as many quarter-cells as the value in $43E3 says are gone, and copies the 64 bytes to the character set at $FAC8.
Adds A to the decimal number of one digit per byte ending at $0A00+X, carrying from digit to digit leftwards.
Draws seven digits from $0A00 onwards into the panel, through the pointer $8B/$8C set to $FA58.
Where the play loop at $179E goes when $1A1E is set; calls $58C8.
Screen-code text of the photo session: "SUBJECT", "PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE", "DARKMAN MUST PREPARE A DISGUISE TO FOOL THE EVIL GANGSTERS", ended by "END OF LINE".

Reached from $4A8F when play ends with $1A1E set: tidies up ($18C5), turns on extended colour mode through $0A5F and $D011, sets $203B to $FF so no fire is seen, and sets pointers to the text at $CD53. The text of the photo session lies just before it, at $57C6.
